meta.title: Make a Paper Rocket
meta.textType: functional: instructions with first, then, next, finally

paragraphs: Tom and Lily want to make a paper rocket for space day at school. You can make one too. Prepare your things before you begin. You need a sheet of paper, scissors, glue, a pencil, and a straw. Tom puts the things on the table in the living room. Pip sits on the floor and watches Tom and Lily. The rocket has four steps, and each step has a picture. "Are you ready?" asks Lily.

First, cut the paper in a long strip. Lily cuts it with the scissors, and Tom holds the paper. Then glue the strip into a round tube. Pull the top off the glue, and put glue on one end of the strip. Tom wants to go on to the next step. "Is the glue dry?" he asks. "Wait," says Lily. "Glue needs time." Pip puts his nose on Tom's foot, and they wait.

Next, make a top for the rocket. Cut a round piece of paper, and make it into a small hat. The hat must have a point at the top. Glue the hat on the tube. Do not finish too fast, because the glue must be dry. Finally, put the rocket on the straw. Blow air through the straw, and the rocket flies!

Tom and Lily stand at the end of the room. Tom blows air through the straw. The rocket flies across the room. Pip runs after it, and Tom laughs. Lily laughs, too. "Can we make a new one?" asks Tom. The last line of the page says, "Next time, make a silver one." "Yes, we can," says Lily. "We will make a silver rocket for space day."
text.summary: Tom and Lily make a paper rocket in four steps. The text says what you need, and the last line asks you to make a silver one next time.
